correctness.rationale: For a first local forcing move, λ−1 neighbour colours in other parts plus its forced colour exhaust the palette, forcing that part monochromatic; hence every polychromatic part must have been completely initially seeded. Two entirely empty monochromatic parts prevent any first move; otherwise the empty part if present forces first, and each remaining blank monochromatic vertex then sees all other colours. Counting surjective colour partitions gives P_G(λ), and selecting seeded subsets in the possible monochromatic parts gives B_t minus the already-counted total assignment; uniqueness of local completion avoids duplicate counting. Optimizing seed counts over admissible extra-colour capacities proves the minimum formula. Independently brute enumerated all initial partial assignments in 48 small parameter cases across 15 multipartite profiles, obtaining 54,346 successful states and exact agreement at every coefficient and minimum. The written general proof, not this finite check, handles arbitrary sizes.

value.rationale: Farr explicitly motivates the difficult regime with surplus palette colours. The new all-palette, r≥3, λ≥r+2 classification includes two or more multicoloured parts, impossible in any previously covered r-palette, one-surplus or bipartite case. It determines the entire domain-size enumerator (not just a minimum) for a natural infinite parameter family, and the minimum seed cost is a nontrivial exact capacity-constrained subset-sum optimization over the actual part sizes. For K_{2,2,3} with λ=5, the theorem predicts the full new coefficient sequence and a minimum of four seeds, independently checked. This adds structural information and optimization phase boundaries of plausible use in graph-polynomial and propagation problems.
